meta.provenance: HAND-AUTHORED BOOTSTRAP plus two single-point real-run measurements (see measured_runs). Not a sweep -- replace with tests/measure_wan_ceiling.py --reduce output before raising any entry beyond what measured_runs supports.
meta.token_law: tokens = ((F-1)/4 + 1) * (H/32) * (W/32); this is ~2x LTX at identical geometry, so attention cost is ~4x. ltx_ceiling.json is NOT a valid prior for Wan.

256x256x9.note: Pre-decode-split smoke test: stage 2 then included the fp32 decode, so 18.75 of the old 20.59 GiB cap is not comparable to post-split numbers.

512x512x49.note: First successful 512x512x49 (run 20260827T035654Z-e1a58899), post decode-split, stage-3 decode at bf16 under torch.no_grad(). Stage-3 driver pool peaked 24.07 of the 24.34 cap -- only 1.1% margin -- while LIVE tensors were just 3.46 GiB: the MPS caching allocator retains freed per-frame decode buffers for the life of the process. FRACTION_STAGE3=0.65 is therefore genuinely required for 512px decode as implemented; do not trim it without re-measuring. Took FIVE failed decode attempts to get here; root cause of all of them was a missing torch.no_grad() around the direct vae.decode() call (linear ~3.7 GiB/2s autograd-graph growth that filled any cap), NOT fragmentation, dtype, tiling, or transformer residency -- see wan_video_skill.py stage-3 comments.
